slides.image_prompt: Elon Musk laughing as a crushed gas car sits worthless and discarded in a junkyard

caption:
Elon Musk says solar will wipe out oil, gas, and nuclear until they're basically nothing. A billionaire's response: 'Probably nothing.'

Everyone assumed solar was growing fast but would always be one option among many. Oil kept the lights on. Gas heated your house. Nuclear was the long-term plan. That was the accepted story.

Then Musk posted on X: solar will keep growing until oil, gas, coal, and nuclear together fall below 0.1% of total energy use. Not shrinking. Not declining. Effectively gone. The tweet got 1.9 million views.

Here's the part that should stop you cold. Chamath Palihapitiya, a billionaire investor who has watched more energy money move than most people will ever see, read a prediction about the literal death of fossil fuels as industries. His public response was two words: 'Probably nothing.' That is not dismissal. That is what insiders say when something is already obvious to them and they want to look calm about it.

If Musk is even close to right, the gas car you're financing right now is on a path to worthless before the loan is paid off. Every oil stock sitting in a retirement account just got a target on its back. And the man making that prediction personally sells solar panels and electric cars. He profits billions if he's right. That doesn't make him wrong.

The world's richest man just called the death of fossil fuels. The only other billionaire who responded said 'probably nothing' and meant the opposite. Oil, gas, and nuclear below 0.1% of total energy. That is the whole story.
